walkthroughs.body_html:
A World Divided: Superpower Relations 1943-72 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

A World Divided: Superpower Relations 1943-72 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with A World Divided: Superpower Relations 1943-72.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What was agreed at the Tehran Conference in 1943?
options: Britain and the USA would open a second front in Western Europe
Germany would be permanently reunified
The USSR would join the Marshall Plan
Berlin would be given entirely to the USSR

mcqs.q: What was the purpose of the Marshall Plan?
options: To provide US economic aid to rebuild Europe and reduce the appeal of communism
To create a military alliance against the USSR
To rebuild Japan's navy
To lend money directly to the Soviet government

mcqs.q: How did the Western powers respond to the Berlin Blockade?
options: They flew supplies into West Berlin in a massive airlift
They blockaded Soviet ports in return
They handed West Berlin to East Germany
They invaded the Soviet zone of Germany

mcqs.q: What did the SALT 1 agreement of 1972 do?
options: Limited anti-ballistic missile systems and froze the number of strategic missile launchers
Banned all nuclear weapons
Ended the Vietnam War
Dissolved the Warsaw Pact

mcqs.q: Was the wartime Grand Alliance based on trust and friendship?
options: The United Nations sent peacekeepers to occupy Cuba.
No - it was a marriage of convenience against Hitler; once Germany was close to defeat, old suspicions over Poland, Germany and ideology resurfaced at Yalta and Potsdam.
The Grand Alliance was a formal union of the American and Soviet governments.
The USA and USSR were close friends who only fell out suddenly after 1945.

mcqs.q: How was the Cuban Missile Crisis actually resolved?
options: The United Nations sent peacekeepers to occupy Cuba.
Kennedy simply forced Khrushchev to back down without giving anything in return.
Detente was a military pact directed against China.
Khrushchev publicly withdrew the missiles in return for a US pledge not to invade Cuba, while Kennedy secretly agreed to remove US missiles from Turkey.

mcqs.q: Did detente mean the USA and USSR became allies?
options: The Grand Alliance was a formal union of the American and Soviet governments.
No - detente was a relaxation of tension through agreements like SALT 1, while rivalry, the arms race and proxy conflicts continued.
Detente was a military pact directed against China.
Detente meant the Cold War was over and the superpowers were now allies.
